knowledge_base_name: YNS-FO-GT SE37 Business Requirements Knowledge Base
purpose: Ground an AI model in the application/business context represented by the supplied SE37 Business Requirement Definition presentations. The model should use these requirements as the source of truth, distinguish business process descriptions from HQ requirements, and avoid inventing requirements that are not present in the source.

application_context.business_solution_context: Microsoft Dynamics 365 Finance & Operations (D365 F&O) business requirements
application_context.scope: End-to-end Finance, Supply Chain, Sales, Procurement, Warehouse, Product, Manufacturing, Warranty and Asset business processes represented in the BRDs.
model_grounding_rules: Treat the supplied BRDs as the primary business source of truth.
Use process codes and function IDs exactly as stated when available.
HQ Requirements are business rules/requirements and should not be weakened or reinterpreted.
Do not invent missing fields, workflows, approvals, integrations, configurations or exceptions.
When a requirement is ambiguous, state that the BRD does not specify the detail.
Keep business terminology such as O2C, P2P, P2Q, A2D and C2R aligned with the BRDs.
When answering a requirement question, identify the relevant business process and requirement ID/slide where possible.
Differentiate standard D365 F&O capability, add-on behavior, interface behavior and business policy when the BRD explicitly does so.

chunks.title: Corporate Structure and Legal Entities
chunks.content:
Corporate Structure and Legal Entities 
Requirement Definition
Legal Entity
A legal entity is an organization that has a registered or legislated legal structure. Legal entities are required to prepare statements that report on their performance. 
A legal entity must follow country specific local business requirements and must provide Financial reporting as per YMC guidelines.

A company is a type of legal entity.
Users can access data only for the company that they are currently signed in to and have security access for the roles they belong to.
Operating Unit
An operating unit is an internal organization that is used to divide the control of economic resources and operational processes in a business.
* Although operating units are optional in finance and operations apps, they're commonly used as financial dimensions(explained later).
HQ Req covered in this slide
HQ Req 105 (P&A): The Company unit is specified for each introduction base. Since the definition will include other departments and accounting, make sure to define the entire implementation project for each site.
HQ Req 108, 110 and 112 (P&A): Business unit can be created in F&O for division of sales organization, business office and purchase organization.

chunks.source_file: YNS-FO-GT_SE37_ Business Requirement Definition_65.Record to Results_v1.00 (1).pptx
chunks.title: Corporate Structure and Legal Entities
chunks.content:
Corporate Structure and Legal Entities 
Requirement Definition
Organization Hierarchies
Organizational hierarchies represent the relationships between the organizations that make up a business. Therefore, the most important consideration when you model organizations is the structure of your business.

For example, you can set up a hierarchy of legal entities for tax, legal, or statutory reporting. Or, you can set up a hierarchy that is based on operating units to report financial information that is not legally required but is used for internal control. For example, you can create a security hierarchy to manage data security policies among various business units.

Decide whether to model internal organizations as legal entities or operating units
Yamaha business eg: Company can be created as Legal Entity, Direct shops can be created as Operating unit of type Business unit
HQ Req covered in this slide
HQ Req 109, 111 and 113 (P&A): Organization hierarchy can be created in F&O for distribution channel, sales group and purchase group.

Derived dimensions
A dimension can also be configured in such a way that information for other dimensions is automatically entered when you enter that dimension in a document (sales order, purchase order etc.). For example, if you enter cost center, ‘Legal’ in a master record or on a document, department ‘HR’ and location ‘Head office’ are entered by default.
Derived Dimension
Financial dimension templates
Some business scenarios require distribution of amounts in source documents like SO, PO based on Financial dimensions.

A template of percentage and financial dimension value combinations can be created. The information in the template will be used to display default financial dimension values when you distribute source document amounts.
Based on this template, the document amount will be distributed among various cost center and business unit.

Chart Of Accounts
Requirement Definition
To create a Chart Of Accounts, It is recommended to follow below concept :
Each account is to be assigned a unique account number. 
Must follow international accounting standard i.e. IFRS
Must follow local government reporting requirements 
In case of group companies, all companies can follow separate COA format or same format, But it must be clear to achieve consolidated reporting.
Specific to Yamaha, must be able to map with G-COA concept for global reporting purpose
Chart of Accounts
(compiled with IFRS and local government requirements)
Balance Sheet (B\S)
Profit & Loss(P\L)
Assets are items owned or controlled by the business, and they have economic value and are used to generate revenue for the firm
Liability accounts provide a list of categories for all the debts that the business owes its creditors.
Revenue accounts record the company’s income from all sources, both earned, such as sales and fees, and unearned, such as investment gains.
Chart of Account| Architecture
Equity referred to as owners' equity for privately held companies, represents the amount of money that would be returned to a company’s owners.
Expenses are recording all money spent, or costs incurred, by a business in their effort to generate revenues.

chunks.title: Chart of Account| Advanced Rules (Account Structure)
chunks.content:
Chart of Account| Advanced Rules (Account Structure)
Chart Of Accounts
Requirement Definition
To support effective controls, Businesses require control at the COA level to run system transactions according to company rules, which can be defined at following level.
MANAGE EXCEPTIONS
Advanced rules can help you manage exceptional conditions. For example, suppose a particular legal entity of your organization needs to behave a little differently than the other ones. In that case, you can use an advanced rule for the subset of that entity and have sorted reporting or maybe remove it.
To allow or not allow blank dimension transactions for ledger account is also an example of Manage exceptions.

ADD Fixed Dimension to Ledger ACCOUNT
You can use an advanced rule to override dimension to the main account or even the subset of the main account. For example, On posting of transaction in revenue G\L, Department dimension always be “SALES”. In this case, Fixed value can be assigned on G\L account to override user input values.

ADD COMBINATION BASED DIMENSION
Advanced rules are also helpful when business need to add new dimension on the basis of combination of specific or range of G\L and Dimensions. It is also use to restrict allow dimension value for specific G\L account. For example, in case of “MC revenue” G\L account, default product type dimension must be “Motor Cycle” and in SP revenue G\L account “Motor Cycle” product type dimension not allowed. 

POSTING VALIDATION
Each G\L account is created in COA to posting some transactions related to business need. There are some accounts where posting is through journal voucher and some G\L accounts transactions are routed through ledger posting in non-finance area i.e. Sales invoice posting, Inventory posting, vendor transactions.
In routed G\L accounts, it is always manual entries restricted.

Types of currencies
A legal entity can deal in multiple currencies for conducting business and these are primarily divided into two heads:
Currency 

In business terms, currency refers to:

Money used as a medium of exchange for goods and services.

A unit of account for budgeting and valuing assets.

A store of value and a standard of value.

A sample currency revaluation example is as follows:
Company A purchases office supplies from Company B on 01/05/2024. Company A’s functional currency is euros and agrees to pay 100,000 EUR for the equipment in 30 days. However, Company B’s functional currency is USD.

Assume that on the date of the transaction agreement, 1 EUR is equivalent to 1 USD (so the exchange rate from EUR to USD is 1).
In this case, here’s the accounting entry that Company B would record on 01/05/2024:

Let’s assume that when Company B closes the books at the period end 31/05/2024, the exchange rate is 1 EUR = 1.5 USD. At this point, currency revaluation will be processed. The original 100,000 USD recorded on May 15th is now worth (revalued at) 150,000 USD on May 31st due to the exchange rate fluctuation. The accounting entry of the revaluation will be as follows:

Company A pays company B on 05/06/2024 (settlement date). If the exchange rate on the settlement date for 1 EUR is now 1.7 USD, the unrealized gain is reversed, and the differences in value are recorded as a realized gain.

Types of Accounting
Accrual Accounting Overview
Accrual accounting involves posting revenue and expenses in the period in which they are earned or incurred, regardless of cash flow timing.
This method provides a more holistic and forward-looking view of company’s financial status.
It focus on matching income with expenses in a financial period.
This method adheres to matching principle for recording transactions.
This method improves transparency and decision making based on more accurate financial performance.
Cash Accounting

Cash basis of accounting records transactions only when the cash is exchanged
Accrual Accounting

Accrual accounting recognizes revenue and expenditure when they are earned or incurred, providing a more comprehensive view of financial performance.
Accruals vs Deferrals
 | Accruals | Deferrals
Meaning | Accruals recognized revenue or expenses when they occur. | Deferrals delay recognition until a future period
Impact | Accruals provide a more accurate representation of financial position. | Deferral result in timing difference in reporting.

Close Month End
Requirement Definition
Month-End Close
The month-end close process is a crucial process that is done at the end of each month to ensure accurate and timely financial reporting. It involves several steps, including reconciling accounts, reviewing transactions, adjusting entries, preparing financial statements, and analyzing performance.
this process serves as a crucial checkpoint in a company’s financial management, allowing for the assessment of performance, planning, and ensuring compliance with regulations.
a well-orchestrated closing process ensures accurate financial reporting, a clear view of the organization's financial health, and a springboard for informed strategic moves.
Month-End Vs Year-End
Month-End Close | Year-End Close
The month-end close focuses on regular assessments and adjustments, enabling businesses to monitor their financial health on an ongoing basis. | Year-end close is a more comprehensive process, culminating in the preparation of annual financial statements for external stakeholders, such as investors and regulatory authorities.

Type | Meaning | Example
Intercompany Debt | Intercompany debt is when there is a loan, payable or receivables between a subsidiary and another subsidiary or the parent company. | If parent company pays for a warehouse that subsidiaries use. In this case, each subsidiary has an expense, but because the parent company paid it, intercompany elimination will be processed.
Intercompany Revenue and Expenses | This elimination is processed when goods or services are bought and sold within the parent company and its subsidiaries because the parent company's consolidated net assets remain unchanged. | When a subsidiary purchase goods from its parent or other subsidiary, then intercompany elimination should be processed. Also, interest or revenue on loans and the cost of goods sold from an intercompany sale will be eliminated.

Requirement Definition
Global Database
A G-DB system has been established as a part of “Yamaha management system” by YMC, which collect business data from each company to G-DB, realize One Fact One Place, then improve group-wide business management.

Currently each group company’s PIC adjusts and sends the data to YMC. This technique has some drawbacks:
 
1. Consolidating data at global level takes time, as different group companies have different logic for allocation. 
2. Only one way communication for each group company. 
3. Low profitability and more action required for this approach. 

In the process, G-DB system follows “One Fact One Place” rule. This unify and realize two- way communication.
 
1. Will increase the profitability and explanation of demand-supply adjustment, globally. 
2. It will establish a two-way communication between Yamaha Group Company and YMC. 
3. Reduce the manual work.

Replenish Warehouse Picking Locations

Inventory Replenishment
Inventory replenishment refers to the process of restocking warehouse shelves from the storage racks to the picking shelves. We can use mobile devices to fulfill Inventory replenishment strategies.

The following replenishment strategies are available:

Wave demand replenishment – This strategy creates replenishment work for outbound orders or loads if inventory isn't available when the wave creates work. For example, replenishment work can be created if the quantity that is required for a sales order isn't available when a wave is processed.

Min/Max replenishment – This strategy uses minimum and maximum stocking limits to determine when locations should be replenished. The item and location criteria define the inventory that is evaluated for replenishment. Min/Max replenishment templates are the primary mechanism for maintaining optimal levels in picking locations. To help guarantee that enough pick face inventory is available to meet wave demand, we can use demand replenishment as a supplement between Min/Max replenishment cycles.

Load demand replenishment – This strategy sums the demand for several loads and creates the replenishment work that is required to stock the relevant picking locations. This strategy helps guarantee that the loads that are created can be picked in the warehouse after they are released.

Immediate replenishment – This strategy replenishes inventory before a wave is run if allocation fails for a location directive line that has a replenishment template.

chunks.title: A Sales Agreement is a contract that commits the customer to buy products in a specific quantity or for a specific amount over time, in exchange for special prices, special discounts, and other special terms, such as payment and delivery terms.
chunks.content:
A Sales Agreement is a contract that commits the customer to buy products in a specific quantity or for a specific amount over time, in exchange for special prices, special discounts, and other special terms, such as payment and delivery terms.
The prices and discounts of the sales agreement override the prices and discounts that are stated in any trade agreements that exist.
The validity period of a sales agreement is defined by the Effective date and Expiration date in the agreement. A customer's sales order qualifies for the agreement terms if the requested ship date of the order is within the validity period. All sales order lines that are linked to a sales agreement contribute to fulfillment of that sales agreement.
Create Sales Agreement
Sales Agreement
Type of Commitments in Sales Agreement
Product quantity commitment
The customer agrees to buy a specific quantity of products.
Product value commitment
The customer agrees to buy specific products for a specific amount.
Product category value commitment
The customer agrees to buy products from a specific sales category for a specific amount.
Value commitment
The customer agrees to buy any product or products in any procurement category for a specific amount.

chunks.title: A blanket sales order represents a framework for a long-term agreement between you and your customer.
chunks.content:
A blanket sales order represents a framework for a long-term agreement between you and your customer.
A blanket order is typically made when a customer has committed to purchasing large quantities that are to be delivered in several smaller shipments over a certain period of time. Often blanket orders cover only one item with predetermined delivery dates. The main reason for using a blanket order rather than a sales order is that quantities entered on a blanket order don't affect item availability and thus can be used as a worksheet for monitoring, forecasting, and planning purposes.

For example: Suppose Company “A” wants to buy 1000 chairs over next 10 months on agreed discounted price with delivery on every first week of month.

chunks.title: Sales Order
chunks.content:
Sales Order
Sales Flow
Create Sales Order; Manual
A Sales order is a document issued by a seller to a buyer, confirming the details of a sale transaction. It outlines the products or services the buyer has agreed to purchase, along with the quantities, prices, terms, and conditions.
Once accepted by both parties, a sales order becomes a legally binding contract, outlining the obligations of both the buyer and the seller. It serves as a reference point for fulfilling the order and resolving any disputes that may arise during or after the transaction.
After receiving a sales order, the seller processes it by picking the ordered items from inventory, packaging them, and arranging for their shipment or delivery to the buyer. This process may involve various departments within the seller's organization, including sales, inventory management, and shipping. Once the order is fulfilled, an invoice is usually generated to request payment from the buyer.

chunks.title: Create Sales Order; Manual
chunks.content:
Create Sales Order; Manual
Charges in Sales Order
Charges are costs or fees that are applied to transactions, typically to account for extra services, expenses, or other related costs.
Automatic charges, which are referred to as auto charges, are applied automatically when we create a sales order or purchase order. We can define auto charges for specific vendors, customers, or items or for groups of vendors, customers, or items. We can also define auto charges that apply to all vendors, customers, or items.
Charge codes are used to track different types of charges (Freight, Carriage and Insurance) and used for accounting entries. To apply charges, we must first define charges codes. To apply auto charges, we need charge codes for accounting entries.
There are different type of categories to apply charges i.e., fixed charge(the charge is entered as a fixed amount), pcs(the charge is based on the unit), percentage(the charge is entered as a percentage), intercompany percent(the charge is entered as a percentage for intercompany orders), external(the charge is calculated by a third-party service that is associated with one or more shipping carriers).
We can apply "Freight", "Insurance", "Usance interest" and "Custom duty“ on sales order by creating corresponding charges code. For example: We create a sales order with the following details shown below:

Allocation of charges on the sales order lines will be as follows:
Sales order | Item | Qty | Unit Price | Total Amount
SO0001 | Headlight | 1 | 100 | 100
SO0001 | Tire | 2 | 30 | 60
We maintain the “Freight” charge code for this sales order with fixed charge value of $50.
Now we allocate the freight charge on the order based on the Net Amount of the sales order lines and to All the lines present.
Sales order | Item | Qty | Unit Price | Total Amount | Charges
SO0001 | Headlight | 1 | 100 | 100 | 31.25
SO0001 | Tire | 2 | 30 | 60 | 18.75
HQ Req covered in this slide
HQ Req 32:Outbound delivery costs in each sales transaction should be regarded as Cost of Sold otherwise gross margin would be fluctuated depending on pricing terms, FOB or CIF.
At least 4 delivery costs, "Freight", "Insurance", "Usance interest" and "Custom duty" which are directly associated with each sales transaction should be posted in COGS

chunks.content:
Sales Order Priority
Allocation Process
Priority of stock allocation will be determined by “Sales order priority for fulfillment” in the sales order. Allocation of sales orders is according to the “Sales order priority for fulfillment” defined on the order as follows:
High-1 will be considered as Emergency sales order.
High-2 will be considered as an Internal sales order.
Sales orders will be prioritized from High to Low. If more than one order has the same priority, then they will be sorted based on the created date and time of the order.
Allocation Direction

Forward: It will start the chain from the ordered item and will only check the items forward from the ordered item. Items in the supersession chain which are before the ordered item will not be checked.
Forward from oldest: It will start the chain from the oldest item in the supersession chain irrespective of the ordered item.

chunks.title: Allocation Process
chunks.content:
Allocation Process
.
A supersession chain is a sequential relationship of items that can replace each other. For example, item B is substituted for item A.

Spares allocation will be used to define the sequence of items that will be used to allocate the item in a sales order. Spares allocation will be performed according to the steps below: 
The supersession chain is according to the “Direction” of the stock allocation directive and iterate all the sequences defined in the matrix and will perform the action defined on the appropriate sequence found for the current item in the chain.
After each iteration, if there is any remaining quantity to be allocated, then supersession chain will shift by one item either in the forward or backward direction according to the “Direction” of the stock allocation directive.
The above step will repeat until either the complete ordered quantity is allocated, or max level is reached.
If there is an item with both sales and purchase is open, then it is denoted by DT0.
If there is an item with purchase is closed and sales is open, then it is denoted by DT1.
If there is an item with both sales and purchase is closed, then it is denoted by DT2.
If there is any quantity left to be allocated after the max level is reached or is no sufficient stock available for any item in the chain, then oldest item with DT0 (Purchase and sales open) will be backordered. If there is no item with DT0 in the chain, then the remaining quantity will be cancelled.
If both sales and purchase for an item is closed (DT2), then its quantity will be cancelled, and its substitute item will be added on sales order having the same price as the original item.

Return Order
Customers can return items for various reasons. For example, an item might be defective, or it might not meet the customer's expectations. The return process starts when a customer issues a request to return an item. After the customer's request is received, a return order is created.
Return Material Authorization (RMA) processing builds on sales order functionality. A RMA is registered as a return order, which is created as a sales order, and may have another sales order associated with it, called a replacement order. Both sales orders link to the originating RMA number.
Return order – To register an RMA, We create a return order, which is a sales order that has the assigned type, Returned order. Any changes that you make to the RMA information is automatically updated in the sales order. Until the return order has the status Open, it will not appear in the list of sales orders. We use RMA to handle the arrival and receipt of the returned items, as well as to authorize a credit only disposition action.

 None – Don't check credit limits. You can override this option for a specific customer by selecting the Mandatory credit limit check box in the Customers page. If you do this, the credit limit is check against the customer balance.

chunks.title: Invoice Sales Order
chunks.content:
Invoice Sales Order
Invoicing Sales Order
An invoice within a sales order serves as a legal document outlining the details of a transaction between a seller and a buyer. It includes specifics such as the quantity, price, and description of the products or services sold. Additionally, it usually includes terms of payment, such as payment due date and accepted methods of payment.
Invoicing within a sales order helps in record-keeping and tracking of transactions for both the seller and the buyer. It provides a reference point for accounting purposes, allowing businesses to track sales, monitor payments, and manage their financial records effectively. Additionally, it helps in maintaining transparency and resolving any disputes that may arise regarding the transaction.

Process Write – Off AR Bad debts
Bad debt is a type of expense that occurs after repayment by a customer (when credit has been extended) is no longer considered to be collectable. In other words, bad debt is an irrecoverable receivable.
Reasons for Bad debts
A bad debt write-off is the process of removing an uncollectible debt from a business’s accounting records. This accounting method acknowledges the loss incurred when a debtor fails to repay a debt. Writing off bad debt ensures that a company’s financial statements accurately reflect the true value of its accounts receivable.

What is Sales Quotation?
Prospect vs Customer
In the business world, a prospect and a customer are two different terms that refer to individuals or entities at different stages of the sales process.
A prospect is an individual or organization that fits a seller’s criteria to be a potential customer. These are individuals or businesses that have shown interest in the products or services but have not yet made a purchase. Prospects are in the early stages, with no prior transactional history. They are often the target of acquisition strategies to guide them towards making their first purchase.
On the other hand, a customer is an individual or entity that has already made a purchase or engaged in a transaction with the company. Customers have an established transactional history, indicating a developed relationship with a business. They often provide feedback based on their experiences, contributing to the improvement of products and services. Customers are the focus of retention strategies to foster loyalty and encourage repeat business.

chunks.content:
Sometimes there is change in buyer and seller terms, therefore sales quotation is updated. There could be many reasons as follows: 
Change in Prospect or Customer Requirements: The prospect or customer may have changed their requirements after the initial quotation was sent. This could include changes in the quantity, type of product, or delivery date.
Pricing Adjustments: The price of products or services may change due to various factors such as changes in market conditions, cost of raw materials, or promotional discounts. Updating the quotation ensures that the prospect or customer is given the most accurate and current pricing information.
Updating Delivery Details: The delivery date or method may need to be updated based on the product availability or the customer’s request.
Adding or Removing Products/Services: The prospect or customer may want to add new products or services or remove some from their order. The quotation needs to be updated to reflect these changes.

chunks.content:
Create Production Order, Manual
Production Order
A production order is a directive to manufacture/ assemble a specific item/ kit in a defined quantity by a certain date. 
It includes details about what will be produced, the quantity to produce, and the planned finish date.
It incorporates a Bill of Materials (BOM). 
Production orders facilitate tracking progress, managing costs, while integrating seamlessly with other modules like inventory, sales, and finance for comprehensive management.
Production Lifecycle
Create 
Production order is created by item number, inventory dimensions, quantity, delivery date etc.
The delivery date indicates when the production order should end to deliver on time. 
It will pick active BOM and business users can also change the BOM.

chunks.source_file: YNS-FO-GT_SE37_ Business Requirement Definition_25_Plan to Produce_P&A_v1.00.pptx
chunks.title: Create Production Order, Manual
chunks.content:
Create Production Order, Manual
2. Estimate
The next step is to estimate the production order. The estimation will run to calculate the estimated cost for production order material and process.
We can view the total cost price per unit for the finished product/ kit. It also contain costs according to the bill of materials.

3. Scheduling
Scheduling will be used to plan the production process.

Release 
The Release step indicates when the production order is released to the production floor and warehouse so that the operators can progress on the production orders.

5. Start
The next step in the production cycle is to start the production order.
We can create the picking list, if required we can post it automatically once the production order is started. 

6. Report as finished
The Report as the finished journal is posted. If you want to adjust the journal, you can manually create a new journal where you can make changes.
The kit inventory status is now "Available physical" in the warehouse.
Once the report as finished is posted, The inventory transaction will be updated for the finished good item with the receipt status "Received".

7. End
Validate the inventory transaction status. Now, the system has updated the Financial date and cost amount for the production order. The receipt status is now purchased for the finished good item. 
The financial impact is posted for the production order, and you can't reverse the production status once the production order is Ended.

chunks.content:
A released production order is an order that has been authorized for production. The term Released is used to describe a state in the production order life cycle, where the production order is available for execution on the production shop floor and for warehouse processes.

The Released state is one state in the production order life cycle. Production orders that are in the Released state are available for execution on the production shop floor and for warehouse processes. The Released state has the following characteristics:
A production order can be changed to the Released state either from the production order or by using a batch process. 
The Released state is the signal for the shop floor operators (operators) to start executing the production jobs on the shop floor.
Production papers, such as route cards, route jobs, and jobs cards provide information about production jobs and can be issued.
For materials that are physically reserved, warehouse work is generated to pick materials for the production order.

Reverse Production Status
If we reverse the status of a production order, the order and all operations that are associated with the production revert to a previous step in the production life cycle. 
For example, a production order has a status of Scheduled, and we change the status back to Created. In this case, we must first change the status to Estimated, which is the status that immediately precedes Scheduled. It can then change the status to the status that you want, Created. 
Note: If your order has reached the Report as finished status, we can still reverse it to an earlier status. However, you must re-run estimation and operations to update the information on the order. This step is required, because any reservations of remaining item consumption and operations resource consumption must also be reset.

chunks.title: A Purchase Agreement is a contract that commits the vendor to buy products in a specific quantity or for a specific amount over time, in exchange for special prices, special discounts, and other special terms, such as payment and delivery terms.
chunks.content:
A Purchase Agreement is a contract that commits the vendor to buy products in a specific quantity or for a specific amount over time, in exchange for special prices, special discounts, and other special terms, such as payment and delivery terms.
The prices and discounts of the purchase agreement override the prices and discounts that are stated in any trade agreements that exist.
The validity period of a purchase agreement is defined by the Effective date and Expiration date in the agreement. A purchase order qualifies for the agreement terms if the requested ship date of the order is within the validity period. All purchase order that are linked to a purchase agreement contribute to fulfillment of that purchase agreement.
Create Purchase Agreement
Purchase Agreement
Type of Commitments in Purchase Agreement
Product quantity commitment
You purchase a specific quantity of a product.
Product value commitment
You purchase a specific currency amount of a product.
Product category value commitment
You purchase a specific currency amount in a procurement category.
Value commitment
You purchase a specific currency amount of any product or products in any procurement category.

chunks.title: A blanket purchase order represents a framework for a long-term agreement between you and your vendor.
chunks.content:
A blanket purchase order represents a framework for a long-term agreement between you and your vendor.
A blanket order is typically made when a buyer has committed to purchasing large quantities that are to be delivered in several smaller shipments over a certain period. Often blanket orders cover only one item with predetermined delivery dates. The main reason for using a blanket order rather than a purchase order is that quantities entered on a blanket order don't affect item availability and thus can be used as a worksheet for monitoring, forecasting, and planning purposes.
Create Purchase Agreement
What is “Blanket Order”?
For example: Suppose Company “A” wants to buy 1000 chairs over next 10 months on agreed discounted price with delivery on every first week of month.
The Blanket order is as follows:-

Purchase Order Creation Process
Charges in Purchase Order Order
Charges are additional costs or fees that are applied to transactions, typically to account for extra services, expenses, or other related costs. 
Automatic charges, which are referred to as auto charges, are applied automatically when we create a sales order or purchase order. We can define auto charges for specific vendors, customers, or items or for groups of vendors, customers, or items. We can also define auto charges that apply to all vendors, customers, or items.
Charge codes are used to track different types of charges (Freight, Carriage and Insurance) and used for accounting entries. To apply charges, we must first define charges codes. To apply auto charges, we need charge codes for accounting entries.
There are different type of categories to apply charges i.e., fixed charge(The charge is entered as a fixed amount), pcs(The charge is based on the unit), percentage(The charge is entered as a percentage), intercompany percent(The charge is entered as a percentage for intercompany orders), external(The charge is calculated by a third-party service that is associated with one or more shipping carriers).

A purchase order approval workflow involves establishing a structured process to ensure that all purchase orders are reviewed, approved, and processed efficiently while maintaining control and compliance.
A workflow has two set of parties: 1. Initiator: An initiator is the party who submit purchase requests.
2. Approver: An approver is the party who approves the purchase order request and then it can be confirmed by initiator of the transaction. There can be multiple level of approvers such as initial approver and secondary approver. A workflow approval request can be sent to different approvers based on a multiple parameters. For Example:

Purchase Order Confirmation
Purchase order confirmation is a key step in the procurement process. It signifies that the purchase order has been approved and is ready to be communicated to the vendor, and it helps to lock in the details of the order for further processing. Canceling a purchase order is a process when a purchase order needs to be terminated before it is processed or fulfilled. It helps ensure that no further actions, such as receiving or invoicing, occur against the order.

There can be several reasons why a purchase order might need to be return to vendor. A vendor return order must be created to return items to vendor which may or may not be referenced to an original purchase order.
Here are some common reasons for purchase order returns:
Damaged Goods: Items received in damaged or defective condition may need to be returned to the supplier for replacement or refund.
Incorrect Items: If the supplier sends the wrong items or quantities that do not match what was ordered, a return may be necessary to obtain the correct items.
Quality Issues: Even if items are not damaged, they may still be returned due to quality issues such as manufacturing defects or subpar materials.
Price Discrepancies: If there are discrepancies between the price agreed upon in the purchase order and the invoiced amount, a return may be initiated to rectify the issue.

chunks.title: Prepayments are amounts paid for by a business in advance of the goods or services being received later. Any payment made in advance can be considered a prepayment.
chunks.content:
Prepayments are amounts paid for by a business in advance of the goods or services being received later. Any payment made in advance can be considered a prepayment.

Organizations might issue prepayments (advance payments) to vendors for goods or services before those goods or services are fulfilled. Two methods can be used to issue prepayments to vendors

Prepayments: 
Organizations that don't want to track prepayments as closely or don't receive a prepayment invoice from their vendor can use prepayment journal vouchers instead of the prepayment invoicing method. You can create prepayment journal vouchers by creating journal entries and marking them as prepayment journal vouchers. For this method, you can't track which prepayments to a vendor are made against which purchase orders. However, you can mark a posted prepayment for settlement against a purchase order.

Prepayment invoicing: 
To minimize risk, you can track prepayments by defining the prepayment on a purchase order. For this method, you must create a prepayment invoice that is associated with a purchase order. This method is referred to as prepayment invoicing. 

A prepayment invoice is a document used to record advance payments from suppliers or clients. It contains the amount to be prepaid on a purchase/sales order and enables user to invoice deposits required from clients.
Prepayment invoices are a standard business practice. A vendor issues prepayment invoices to require a deposit on the purchase before the purchase order is fulfilled. For example, some vendors require a prepayment for custom goods or services. If a vendor issues an invoice that requests prepayment, you can use the prepayment invoicing feature in Dynamics 365 F&O.

Segregation of duties
You can set up rules to separate tasks that must be performed by different users. This concept is named segregation of duties. Segregation of duties helps you reduce the risk of fraud, and it also helps you detect errors or irregularities. You can also use segregation of duties to enforce internal control policies. 

For example, you might not want the same person to post invoice and to process payment to the vendor. 

Note: 1. User A and User B can be from the same department on same level of hierarchy.
2. User A and User B can be from the same department on different levels of hierarchy.

Vendor Payment Approval
Vendor payment approval involves a process for ensuring that payments to vendors are authorized and properly managed within an organization. This process helps ensure financial accuracy, compliance with company policies, and vendor satisfaction.

A payment approval workflow is a structured process for reviewing and authorizing payments within an organization. This workflow helps ensure that payments are made accurately, in compliance with company policies, and with appropriate oversight.
A workflow has two set of parties: 1. Initiator: An initiator is the party who creates a payment transaction and initiates a workflow for approval. An initiator should not have the authority to approve the transaction.
2. Approver: An approver is the party who approves the payment and then it can be posted by initiator of the transaction. There can be multiple level of approvers such as initial approver and secondary approver. A workflow approval request can be sent to different approvers based on a multiple parameters. For Example:

For instance, a payment transaction of 500 JPY for a local BP(vendor) may be approved as follows:

Product
A “Product" refers to any tangible goods or services that are part of the inventory managed within the supply chain.
A product in supply chain management consists of a core product definition. This product is defined independent of the organization where it is used. 
Product definitions are created independently of a legal entity. Therefore, core values such as product number, type, and name are shared. 
A Product is created in the product master and each product has its own unique product number. 
A Spare part is an item in product master which does not have a unique identification number and cannot be tracked during normal course of business.
A kit is an item which assembled by grouping a set of items (Spare items).
There are two subtypes of products:

Product - A product is a uniquely identifiable product. It serves as a core product that does not vary; therefore, no product dimensions can be associated with the definition. Spare parts are created as products in product master without any tracking dimension.

Product master - A product master holds the definition and rules that specify how distinct products are described and behave in business processes. Based on these definitions, we can generate distinct products. These distinct products are known as product variants. A product master is associated with one or more product dimensions and product variants. Therefore, units are created as a product master to create variants of a product.

The system will support configurable Product Lifecycle States to control item transactions throughout different stages of the product lifecycle. These states will govern whether an item is allowed for purchase , sales transactions and stock allocation in the system.
Product Lifecycle state
Product lifecycle state | Description
DT0 –Discontinue type 0 | Items with lifecycle state DT0 are fully active in the system.
 All transactions are enabled, and such items can be purchased, sold, and allocated from stock without any restriction.
DT1 –Discontinue type 1 | Items with lifecycle state DT1 are not eligible for purchase in the system.
 During sales order processing, the system shall evaluate inventory availability at the time of stock allocation. If sufficient inventory is not available, and the item is blocked for future purchase due to the DT1 lifecycle state, the system shall either allocate a configured substitute item (Item change) or prevent sales order processing by displaying an appropriate error message.
DT2 –Discontinue type 2 | Items with lifecycle state DT2 are fully blocked for both purchase and sales in the system. 
When a user attempts to create or process a purchase order or a sales order for such items, the system shall validate the lifecycle state and prevent the transaction by displaying an appropriate error message.

The costing method that can be used for inventory valuation are as follows:
40
40
Costing Methods
Costing method | Description | When to use
FIFO | An item's unit cost is the actual value of any receipt of the item, selected by the FIFO rule.
Inventory valuation assumes that the first items placed in inventory are sold first. | In business environments where product cost is stable. For items with a limited shelf life, because the oldest goods need to be sold before they pass their sell-by date.
LIFO | An item's unit cost is the actual value of any receipt of the item, selected by the LIFO rule.
Inventory valuation assumes that the last items placed in inventory are sold first. | When prices are rising, the value on the income statement decreases. This means that tax liabilities decrease, but the ability to borrow cash deteriorates.
Weighted Average | An item's unit cost is calculated as the average unit cost at each point in time after a purchase.
Inventory valuation assumes that all inventories are sold simultaneously. | In business environments where product cost is unstable. When inventories are piled or mixed and can't be differentiated, such as chemicals.
LIFO Date | LIFO date is a variant on LIFO. In this case the LIFO principle (Last in, First out) is followed, but the 'Last in' is based on the last purchase value before the sales posting was made. | In business environment it helps to manage inventory cost flow during financial reporting. Useful when specific date-based cost tracking is required.
Weighted Average Date | An item’s unit cost is calculated as the average value of all the receipt upto the date of issue. | In business environments where product cost is unstable. 
When inventory value is needed upto a date of purchase.
Moving Average | In Moving average no inventory closing is used. After each transaction immediately an average cost price is calculated (therefore a moving average in stead of a weighted average). | In business environments, When average cost price is needed to calculate after each purchase due to purchase price fluctuation.
Standard | An item's unit cost is preset based on estimated.
When the actual cost is realized later, the standard cost must be adjusted to the actual cost through variance values. | Where cost control is critical. In repetitive manufacturing, to value the costs of direct material, direct labor, and manufacturing overhead. Where there's discipline and staff to maintain standards.

chunks.title: Moving Average
chunks.content:
Moving Average
Moving average is a perpetual costing method based on the average principle.

How It Works:

Initial Calculation: Start with the cost and quantity of the existing inventory.
New Purchase: When new inventory is purchased, add the cost and quantity to the existing inventory.
New Average Cost: Recalculate the average cost per unit by dividing the updated total cost by the updated total quantity.

Moving average method in D365 F&O have the following distinctive features: 
The costs on inventory issues do not change when the purchase cost does. The difference is capitalized and is based on a proportional calculation. The amount that remains is expensed; and do not impact COGS account.

Adjustment of charges, if any, does not capitalize in item cost. The amount will be posted to the price difference expense account; and do not impact COGS account.

Inventory adjustment does not adjust the item cost and hence only quantity can be adjusted at current moving average cost of the item.

Detail of above scenarios are explained in below slides.

ABC Classifications of Inventory Requirement Definition
74
What is ABC Classification of Inventory?
ABC inventory analysis is a commonly used strategy to categorize inventory into “A”, “B”, and “C” classifications based on the Pareto Principle that 80% of sales, cost, or inventory value can be attributed to 20% of the products in inventory. This classification helps businesses prioritize and gear processes toward their most profitable or valuable inventory items.
ABC classification not only allows us to calculate and display the ABC classification associated to the product based on user defined parameters, but also to automatically assign to those classifications to products. This allows us to do reporting and analytics based on this assignment as well as other things like, cycle count frequency, and even different warehouse processes.
ABC Report Parameters
1. Revenue: This option will calculate the ABC classification based on the revenue generated by the product. This means sales data will be used to determine how much revenue was generated during a given time period for this product.
2. Margin: This option will also use sales and cost data during the specified time period to determine the margin of the product.
3. Value: This option will calculate use the product’s inventory value by multiplying the cost by the quantity on hand to determine inventory value.
4. Carrying cost: This option will calculate product carrying cost. The carrying cost calculates how much it costs to carry the inventory based on a given interest rate that could be earned by investing the money into a secured one year or guaranteed asset like treasury bonds or certificate of deposit. 
Carrying cost = ((annual interest rate / 365) * days the product was carried in inventory)

Warranty provision posting and reconciliation
Provision Posting and Reconciliation
Provision Posting
Warranty provision posting refers to the process of setting aside a specific amount of money in a company's financial records to cover potential future costs related to warranty claims. 
Since warranties involve a promise to repair or replace a product if it fails within a certain period, businesses need to anticipate the costs they might incur for these repairs or replacements.

Provision Entry: When a warranty is offered, the company creates a provision entry in their accounting records. This entry ensures that funds are set aside for covering future claims, even if no claims have been made yet.

Adjustments: As warranty claims are made and the company incurs actual costs, the provision is reduced. If more claims occur than expected, the provision may need to be increased.
Reconciliation
Our system provides a warranty provision report used for the warranty provision reconciliation process. 
This report is generated on a scheduled basis, such as monthly or quarterly, and is compared against the relevant accounts. 
Any discrepancies identified between the report and the accounts must be manually reviewed and analyzed.

Creation of a recall/service campaign
Recall/Service Campaign
71
Recall / Service Campaign
A recall is an action taken by a manufacturer or regulatory authority to remove a product from the market due to safety concerns, defects, or non-compliance with standards.
 In a recall, customers are usually notified and offered a remedy, which could involve repairing, replacing, or refunding the affected product.
A service campaign is issued by the manufacturer to address units defects that arise after the sale.
It involves service repairs due to the manufacturer's fault.
The campaign notifies customers about the defects needing repair.
When a customer responds to the notification and arrives at the service reception, a work order can be generated based on the service campaign information.
SCENARIO

During routine quality testing and customer complaints, Marine Tech discovered a fuel system defect in the X200 model caused by a faulty fuel injection valve, leading to potential fuel leaks under certain conditions. 
This defect could result in engine failure or fire, especially in saltwater environments. Although no serious injuries have been reported, several customers have experienced poor engine performance and high fuel consumption. 
To ensure safety, Marine Tech has decided to recall all X200 models sold in the past 18 months and replace the defective valve free of charge.

Service campaign types
 There are three types of Service campaign:
Emergency (the customer needs to be notified immediately to repair the fault as soon as possible)
Security (the fault is fixed during the next service visit)
Service (it is not essential to repair the fault and is repaired only if the customer complains)

Service campaign line
 Service campaign lines represent all units to which the service campaign is attached.

Notification letter
 A notification letter is used to inform the customer that its units needs to be repaired due to a manufacturer fault. The notification letter form defines the structure of a Service campaign letter.

Service campaign letter journal
 The service campaign letter journal is used to send letters or e-mails to those custodians or customers that have not yet responded to previously sent letters

Depreciation & Amortization of Fixed Asset
Depreciation Depreciation refers to the systematic allocation of the cost of tangible assets over their useful life to reflect their reducing value due to wear and tear, obsolescence, or other factors.
Amortization
 Amortization is the cost of spreading the cost of intangible assets, like patents or trademarks, over a specific time period to reflect their diminishing value as they are consumed or used.
In dynamics 365 finance and operation, depreciation and amortization are crucial for proper financial reporting and compliance with the accounting standards. Understanding and correctly applying these concepts is vital for accurate asset valuation and financial statement preparation.
